detail.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation via Hybrid Architectures and Goal Generation
detail.summary: Autonomous discovery systems require self-healing mechanisms and meta-strategies to navigate iterative research. While computational complexity (cascading dependencies) serves as a baseline for measuring project difficulty, evaluating true scientific significance requires incorporating metrics that model the development of analytical thinking and curiosity, as seen in physics education.
detail.reason: Integrating findings from physics outreach literature (source-52719ea4691d44b7) suggests that scientific significance is not merely about complexity, but about the inquiring mindset.

detail.title: Autonomous Problem Formulation and Investigation
detail.question: Can an intelligent process independently identify a worthwhile problem that nobody explicitly assigned, recognize its significance, and sustain an investigation toward resolving it?
detail.reason: Literature synthesis completed; establishing a mechanism to validate the proposed evaluation framework is the logical next step.
